identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian-built Fiat Uno, produced from 1984 and classed by AMS2 under Copa Classic B. The first generation was offered with four- or five-speed manual gearboxes, the five-speed being Ritmo/Strada-derived.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.
The only D-shaped rim in this batch; the other five cars carry round wheels.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.uno-classic-b.20260814t181826261z-af324a9f by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the Uno and its gearbox options, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The source lists 4- or 5-speed manual transmissions and a Ritmo/Strada-derived five-speed, and the live drive selected five H-pattern gears. An ordinary production road-car manual of this period is synchronised.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: The first-generation Uno was offered with four- or five-speed manuals, and the drive found the Ritmo/Strada-derived five-speed. Synchronised is the ordinary reading of a road-derived manual rather than a stated specification, so the blip eases it but should not be needed.
